podcast.title: "46 and 2" Chromosome Theory
podcast.body: James Keenan stated that the song "46 and 2" alludes to the idea that humans will eventually evolve from having 46 chromosomes to 48, a concept based on the theories of Carl Jung. "which according to Maynard, alludes to how humans will eventually evolve from having 46 chromosomes to 48."

podcast.title: Attempted Tapeworm Collaboration
podcast.body: James Keenan made an attempt to form a band called Tapeworm with Trent Reznor, but the project ultimately did not work out. "Made it work with the perfect circle, and tried to form a band with Trent Rezner called Tapeworm that didn't work out."

xref.title: Supergroup Lineup and Origins (1994-2001)
xref.body: Tapeworm was conceived as a side project during Nine Inch Nails' "The Downward Spiral" sessions in 1994, intended as a collaborative effort for Danny Lohner and Charlie Clouser. It evolved to include a star-studded lineup: Trent Reznor, Maynard James Keenan (Tool), producer Alan Molder, Atticus Ross, Phil Anselmo and Rex Brown (Pantera), Page Hamilton (Helmet), Toni Halliday (Curve), Tommy Victor (Ministry), and drummer Josh Freese, with at least an album's worth of material recorded by 2001. "If you're Trent Rezner, Danny Loaner and Charlie Closer from his live band, Maynard James Keenan from Tool, producer Alan Molder and Atticus Ross. I mean, wow, awesome, right? The idea for tapeworm went as far back as the sessions for the downward spiral in 1994. Tapeworm was designed as something to which Danny and Charlie could contribute as equals. This idea evolved into something pretty cool. Maynard was brought in, Phil and Salmo from Pantera, Paige Hamilton from Helmut, Tony Haliday from a cool band called Curve, Tommy Victor from Ministry, drummer Josh Freeze. And then in 2001, Alan Molder apparently helped record at least an album's worth of stuff."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Project History (1995-2004)
xref.body: This project was created in 1995 and involved Trent Reznor, Atticus Ross, and a variety of friends, continuing off and on for nine years. Despite the collaboration, nothing was ever officially released. "I already mentioned the tapeworm project, which was created in 1995 and included a lot of different friends. They were continued off and on for nine years, but nothing was ever released."

xref.title: Full-Time Recording and Touring Outfit
xref.body: A Perfect Circle was formed by Maynard James Keenan as a brand new, full-time recording and touring outfit, securing a contract with a completely different record label. Keenan's commitments to this band immersed him in recording, which in turn delayed the creation of Tool's third album. "Mayor joined what appeared to be a brand new, full-time recording and touring outfit, with a contract with a completely different label."

xref.title: Guitar Tech for Tool, Co-founded A Perfect Circle
xref.body: Billy Howerdel initially worked as a guitar tech for the band Tool. During Tool's downtime, he co-founded A Perfect Circle, a band that features Tool's lead singer, Maynard James Keenan. "Billy Howardale was a guitar tech for tool. When they weren't doing anything he played in a perfect circle featuring tool singer Maynard James Keenan."

xref.title: Instrumental in Forming Tool
xref.body: Tom Morello played a crucial role in the formation of the band Tool by introducing his former classmate Adam Jones and Jones's new friend, singer Maynard James Keenan, to drummer Danny Carey. "Meanwhile, Adam Jones, who had also moved west, was looking to form his own band. Tom introduced Adam and his new friend, singer, Maynard James Keenan, to a drummer named Daddy Kerry. So, yeah, Tom basically put two all together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Maynard James Keenan's Family Winemaking Heritage
xref.body: Maynard James Keenan, known for his work in Tool, A Perfect Circle, and Puscifer, has a family history in winemaking, with relatives in northern Italy who he believes still make wines. This heritage influenced his own venture into viticulture. "His family still might make wines in northern Italy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Maynard's Other Band
xref.body: Puscifer is Maynard James Keenan's other musical project, active during periods when he was not working with Tool. "When he wasn't working with Tool, Maynard had his other band, Pussifer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Merkin Vineyards and Caduceus Cellars – Maynard James Keenan's Arizona Wine Operations
xref.body: Maynard James Keenan owns Merkin Vineyards and Caduceus Cellars, high-end wine operations located in the Sedona area of Arizona, specifically in Cornville, north of Phoenix and south of Flagstaff off I-17. He invested money earned from Tool and A Perfect Circle into these ventures. Merkin refers to a wig worn in the pubic region, while Caduceus, the ancient symbol for commerce, is associated with the brand's website, www.cadocious.org. His wines, particularly the '84 cab blend, have received excellent reviews, and the tasting center invites wine lovers to sample and purchase. "Maynard owns Merckin Vineyards."

xref.title: Record Label Disinterest in Tapeworm
xref.body: The record labels for both Nine Inch Nails and Maynard James Keenan were reportedly "not keen" on the Tapeworm project. This lack of label support, along with scheduling conflicts and internal band dynamics, ultimately prevented the album from being released, despite recording sessions in New Orleans and Atlanta in 2003. "But then reality set in. 9 inch nails record label and Maynard's labels weren't keen on the idea."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Trent Reznor's Rehab and Recovery
xref.body: After the Tapeworm project faced challenges, Trent Reznor entered rehab. Upon his recovery, he expressed a desire to refocus on Nine Inch Nails, a decision that further impacted the viability and completion of the Tapeworm album, especially given Maynard James Keenan's commitments to other bands. "Meanwhile, Trent went into rehab. And when he recovered, he wanted to get back into 9 inch nails."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
